name: FixLabs Content Freshness
author: fixlabs

sections.description:
Old posts quietly lose rankings. A title that says “Best Laptops 2023”, a net worth figure “as of 2024” or a guide nobody has touched in two years tells readers and search engines that your content is out of date.

FixLabs Content Freshness shows you exactly which posts need attention, so you can update the ones that matter first.

Features

  • Freshness dashboard – every post sorted from oldest to newest update, with a clear Fresh, Ageing or Stale badge.
  • Outdated year finder – flags posts that mention a past year in the title, or in phrases like “as of 2024”, “updated 2023” or “2024 net worth”.
  • Smart about history – only recent years count in titles, and years more than 15 years old are ignored in content, so names like “London 2012 Olympics” and birth years in biographies are not flagged by mistake.
  • Your own rules – choose when a post counts as ageing and when it is stale (for example 6 and 12 months).
  • Mark as reviewed – checked a post and nothing needs changing? One click resets its freshness clock without editing the post.
  • Freshness column – see each post’s status right on your normal Posts screen.
  • Dashboard widget – a quick count of stale and ageing posts every time you log in.
  • Works with pages and custom post types.
  • Lightweight – no external services, no tracking, nothing loaded on the front end of your site.

Who is it for?

Bloggers, niche and affiliate sites, news and magazine sites, and content teams with more than a handful of posts.

Privacy

This plugin does not collect, store or send any personal data. It does not connect to any external service.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or search for “FixLabs Content Freshness”.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open Content Freshness in the admin menu. The first scan starts automatically.
  4. Adjust the ageing and stale months under Content Freshness → Settings if you like.
sections.faq:
Does it change my posts?

No. It only reads your posts and stores its own notes about them. “Mark reviewed” never changes the post or its modified date.

Will it flag birth years in biographies?

No. In post content only years used in “freshness” phrases are flagged (“as of 2024”, “updated 2024”, “2024 net worth”, “best … 2024”). Years more than 15 years ago are ignored everywhere.

Does it slow down my site?

No. Nothing runs on the front end. Posts are scanned in small batches in the admin, and each post is rescanned when you save it.

Who can see the freshness dashboard?

Editors and administrators. Only administrators can change the settings.

What happens on 1 January?

When the year changes, the plugin asks you to rescan so last year is now counted as outdated.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

All its settings and notes are removed from your database.
